correctness.rationale: All domains and quantifiers specified: positive finite subcatchment volumes, w>1, exact common Fu response, n>=2, local perturbations with conserved totals. Minkowski gives existence/equality; strictly negative derivative of pooled norm in its exponent gives uniqueness. A homogeneous Hessian Taylor expansion gives the exact quadratic contrast and an implicit inversion gives the w-bias. A convergent entropy series proves sharp upper coefficient uniquely at pooled P=D for nonzero mismatch. The strict P-gradient ordering gives two-region global monotonicity. The shipped standard-library checker reproduces 6000 numerical configurations, 27 equality cases, 24 local asymptotic comparisons, 9 monotonicity grids and the exact radical benchmark. The proof does not rely on finite evidence.

value.rationale: Spatially aggregated precipitation/runoff/potential-evaporation data are routinely used for hydrological calibration. A false parameter shift can be mistaken for a vegetation or soil effect even if every local parameter is identical. The theorem supplies the entire sign/equality map, a computable leading contrast energy across arbitrarily many subregions, a sharp regime-independent coefficient, and a unique balanced-climate attainment condition. It is not merely a textbook triangle inequality renamed: the second-order calibrated-parameter sensitivity and sharp aridity-envelope quantify a concrete modeling confounder. No empirical effectiveness is claimed.
